Summary of a VLMC with covariates

Source: R/summary_covlmc.R
summary.covlmc.Rd

This function computes summary statistics of a VLMC with covariates, which are displayed by the associated print() method.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'covlmc'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.covlmc'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

a fitted VLMC with covariates (a covlmc object).

...

additional arguments (not used).

x

a summary of a VLMC with covariates, as returned by summary().

Value

summary() returns an object of class summary.covlmc, a list with the following components:

  • state_space: the state space of the model;

  • nb: the number of contexts;

  • depth: the length of the longest context;

  • avg_depth: the average length of the contexts;

  • alpha: the cut off of the model in quantile scale;

  • covariates: the names of the covariates;

  • no_cov: the number of contexts whose model does not use the covariates;

  • avg_hsize: the average length of the memory of the covariates (see covariate_memory()), computed on the contexts whose model uses the covariates (NaN if there is none);

  • max_hsize: the longest memory of the covariates (see covariate_depth());

  • delta: the average difference between the length of a context and the memory of its model, computed on the contexts whose model uses the covariates (NaN if there is none).

print() displays the summary and returns x invisibly.

See also

covlmc(), contexts.covlmc(), context_number.covlmc(), depth(), covariate_depth()

Examples

pc <- powerconsumption[powerconsumption$week == 5, ]
rdts <- cut(pc$active_power,
  breaks = c(0, quantile(pc$active_power, probs = c(1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1)))
)
rdts_cov <- data.frame(day_night = (pc$hour >= 7 & pc$hour <= 17))
m_cov <- covlmc(rdts, rdts_cov, min_size = 5)
summary(m_cov)
#> VLMC with covariates context tree on (0,0.556], (0.556,1.78], (1.78,7.54] 
#>  Covariates: day_night 
#>  Cutoff in quantile scale: 0.05
#>  Number of contexts: 5 
#>  Contexts without covariate: 3 
#>  Maximum context length: 2 
#>  Average context length: 1.6 
#>  For nodes with covariates: 
#>   Maximum covariate history length: 2 
#>   Average covariate history length: 1.5 
#>   Average difference between context length and history length: 0
